clues: This postively charged protein was discovered in 1869 by a Swiss biochemist who was working with salmon sperm. It is still purified from salmon sperm or testes so the FDA recommends caution with use of this medication in those with fish allergies although cross-reactivity is rare
This protein is combined with insulin to delay the absorption and prolong the effects of insulin

What does NPH stand for? If a patient has been on NPH long term, they can develop antibodies to this component and are at much higher risk of adverse reaction when this medication is administered, such as during cardiac bypass surgery or carotid endarterectomy

Willowbrook State School was a overcrowded and underfunded institution for mentally disabled children. Because diseases were already so endemic, researchers justified deliberately exposing newly admitted children to this blood borne disease to better study it. The public outcry led to sweeping reforms and ultimately influenced the creation of IRBs

In the 19th and early 20th century, outbreaks of this disease were linked to receiving vaccines. For example, in 1942, over 50,000 US soldiers developed this disease after receiving the yellow fever vaccine, which contained human serum

Vaccination against this DNA virus made medical history as the first ever anti-cancer vaccine. First deployed universally in Taiwan in 1984, it slashed childhood rates of a specific type of cancer by 75% within 2 decades.
This organ is the driving force behind amphibian metamorphosis. Abnormalities can lead to an inability for tadpoles to transform into frogs
Typically weighing only 25 grams, any weighing over 250 grams are defined as 'massive'. The largest removed from a human weighed an astonishing 5.2kg
Although commonly described as butterfly shaped, the name of this is derived from a Greek word (θυρεός) meaning 'shield'

The organism causing this disease is suspected to have evolved in the Mesozoic era prior to the breakup of the supercontinent Pangaea. It has plagued humanity since antiquity, with pre-Incan pottery depicting facial disfigurements and lesions caused by the disease

During the massive global push to eradicate malaria in the 1950s, the World Health Organization sprayed widespread amounds of DDT, which inadvertently wiped out some species that transmit the visceral version of this disease

Currently, cutaneous versions are the most common presentation transmitted via the bites of infected female sandflies. Although this disease is found in 98 countries, 90% of new cases occur in just 13 countries.

The early clinical and pathological study of this disease is linked to Dr. Oppenheim, a neurologist, in the early 20th century, who later faced severe religious persecution leading up to the Holocaust
This disease can cause transient focal neurologic episodes, brief disturbances in motor, sensory, visual, or language functions that can be difficult to distinguish from TIAs or seizures
It's not Alzheimers. This disease is caused by amyloid proteins that deposit into the arteries and arterioles in the brain, causing memory issues and increasing the risk of bleeding events
